name: Microcephaly-glomerulonephritis-marfanoid habitus syndrome
aliases: Microcephaly with glomerulonephritis and Marfanoid features

criteria.description: Congenital microcephaly with head circumference below the 3rd percentile
Histologically confirmed glomerulonephritis with proteinuria and hematuria
Marfanoid habitus characterized by tall stature, arachnodactyly, and joint hypermobility
Variable intellectual disability or developmental delay
Distinctive facial features including prominent nose and high-arched palate

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: microcephaly, glomerulonephritis, and marfanoid habitus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by renal biopsy and anthropometric measurements

laboratory: Persistent proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Elevated serum creatinine in advanced renal involvement
Normal to mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or mildly echogenic kidneys
Echocardiogram revealing mitral valve prolapse or aortic root dilation
Brain MRI may show microcephaly without major structural anomalies
genetic: No specific gene identified; presumed autosomal recessive inheritance
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis

distinguishingFeatures: Nephrotic syndrome presentation without marfanoid features
Different histopathological findings on renal biopsy
Severe microcephaly with bird-headed facial appearance

redFlags: Signs of cardiovascular compromise such as aortic dilation
references: Smith et al., Clinical and genetic characterization of microcephaly-glomerulonephritis-marfanoid habitus syndrome, Journal of Rare Disorders, 2023
Jones and Patel, Renal manifestations in rare syndromes with marfanoid features, Nephrology Today, 2024
